title: “I WISH I WAS NEVER BORN.”
paragraphs: “I WISH I WAS NEVER BORN.”

Yes.
That’s in the Bible.

And it wasn’t written by a pagan king or a godless rebel.
It came from the mouth of a prophet.
From the lips of Jeremiah — the weeping messenger of God.
Open your Bible to Book of Jeremiah chapter 20.
And brace yourself.
He Preached Fire. He Got Punched.
Jeremiah didn’t compromise. He didn’t soften the blow. He declared judgment exactly as the Lord commanded.
So what happened?
The priest Pashhur had him beaten. Publicly humiliated. Locked in stocks overnight like a criminal.
Picture it.

Wood cutting into swollen wrists.
Dust clinging to sweat.
Spit in his beard.
Eyes burning from shame.
He was faithful.
And it cost him everything.
“O LORD, You Deceived Me…”
Jeremiah explodes in raw prayer (Jeremiah 20:7).

He accuses.
He weeps.
He rages.
“I am in derision daily… everyone mocks me.”
This is not polished faith.
This is breakdown faith.
And then he says it:
“Cursed be the day I was born… Why did I come out from the womb to see labor and sorrow?” (Jer. 20:14–18)
The prophet of God wished he had never existed.
Let that sink in.
The Fire He Couldn’t Quit
But here’s the line that turns the entire chapter:
“His word was in my heart like a burning fire shut up in my bones; I was weary of holding it back, and I could not.” (Jer. 20:9)
He tried to quit.
He couldn’t.
Because the call of God is not a contract you clock in and out of. It’s a fire that owns you.
Brother, sister — some of you know this feeling.

You’re exhausted.
Misunderstood.
Mocked for your obedience.

And secretly you whisper:
“I wish I wasn’t here.”
The Pivot — From Breakdown to Battle Cry
Right in the middle of the storm, Jeremiah declares:
“But the LORD is with me as a mighty, awesome One.” (Jer. 20:11)
Don’t miss it.

He feels crushed — yet he clings.
He feels betrayed — yet he believes.
Faith is not the absence of emotional collapse.
Faith is clinging to God inside the collapse.
Jeremiah’s breakdown did not cancel his calling.
And Now We Go to the Cross
Because Jeremiah’s cry echoes another cry centuries later.
On a hill outside Jerusalem, another faithful Servant was beaten, mocked, and publicly shamed.
This time it was not a priest striking a prophet.
It was sinners crucifying the Son.

Jesus Christ bore humiliation without sin.
He carried sorrow without rebellion.
He drank the full cup of wrath Jeremiah only tasted.
And on that cross, Jesus entered the darkness of human despair so that your breakdown would never be your burial.
Jeremiah said, “Cursed be the day I was born.”
Jesus became a curse for us (Galatians 3:13) — so that the day of your new birth would be blessed.
That’s the Gospel.

Your pain is real.
Your despair is not hidden.
But your story is not over.
If You’re There Right Now…
If you’ve whispered, “I wish I wasn’t born…”
Hear me as a shepherd.

That thought does not disqualify you from God’s love.
It reveals how deeply you need His grace.

Bring the curse.
Bring the anger.
Bring the tears.
Jesus already carried worse.

Repent of unbelief.
Cling to Christ.
Let His Spirit rekindle the fire in your bones.

Because the same God who sustained Jeremiah
is the God who raised Jesus from the dead.
And resurrection is louder than despair.
Come back to Him today.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
